title: Find out whether turn-gated control works end to end and what a host can configure
outcome: Greg knows, from evidence in the code and the live stores, which control assurance modes Engram defines, which of them TermAl can select or only match, whether a turn-gated session actually mediates turns today, and what is missing or broken, with each gap filed as its own item.
acceptance: every gap found is filed as its own item with its evidence; nothing is changed without Greg's decision
the modes Engram defines (required assurance, mechanical basis, evaluation modes) and the command that sets each are listed from the code, not from memory
what TermAl can configure for Engram, and what it can only match against the store's policy, is listed from TermAl's code
whether turn-gated control mediates a real turn is established from the live stores' control records and an exercised path, with the evidence cited

completion.summary: Established from code and both live stores: the modes Engram defines and the operator commands that set them; what TermAl configures (machine-scoped developer name, binary, home, boot budget; per project only enabled and the turn-gated toggle), matches (required assurance), displays (required assurance after Verify) and cannot change (any store policy); and that turn-gated control has mediated no turn since 2026-09-03 because engram control refused the --actor-context TermAl passes. Seven gaps filed with evidence. Closed on an independent-session evaluation produced by TermAl (third attempt; the first two failed criterion 3 and the record was corrected each time).
